title: PE: extended treatment without a major reversible trigger
summary: After a first acute PE without a major reversible risk factor, continue anticoagulation beyond the initial 3–6 months.
population: First acute PE; no major reversible trigger
evidenceNote: Original recommendation class and evidence level retained.
cautions: Reassess bleeding risk, preferences and ongoing eligibility; this is not a fixed lifelong prescription.

title: PE: stopping after a major reversible trigger
summary: For a first PE caused by a major reversible factor, stop anticoagulation after the initial 3–6-month phase.
population: First acute PE; major reversible trigger
evidenceNote: Original recommendation class and evidence level retained.
cautions: Confirm the trigger category and any separate indication for anticoagulation.

title: PE: shared decision after a minor reversible trigger
summary: After initial 3–6-month treatment, use shared decision-making about stopping versus extending anticoagulation.
population: First acute PE; minor reversible trigger
evidenceNote: Original recommendation class and evidence level retained.
cautions: Balance recurrence and bleeding risks; minor and major triggers have different pathways.

title: LAAO when oral anticoagulation is contraindicated
summary: Consider LAAO rather than no stroke-prevention treatment in nonvalvular AF with an OAC contraindication.
population: Nonvalvular AF; contraindication to oral anticoagulation
evidenceNote: Very low certainty evidence.
cautions: Discuss procedural risk and patient preferences. Benefit may be inappropriate with less than 1 year of quality life expectancy.

title: LAAO: postprocedure antithrombotic options
summary: Postprocedural OAC or dual antiplatelet therapy are suggested options after LAAO.
population: Nonvalvular AF after LAAO
evidenceNote: Low certainty evidence for OAC or DAPT; single-antiplatelet therapy is a knowledge gap.
cautions: Regimen and duration require the implanting team; no single-antiplatelet regimen is endorsed here.

title: Cilostazol: avoid with heart failure
summary: Do not administer cilostazol for PAD when heart failure of any severity is present.
population: PAD with heart failure
evidenceNote: Original recommendation class and evidence level retained.
cautions: Reference only; eligibility and contraindications require individual review.

title: Claudication: pentoxifylline has no recommended role
summary: Pentoxifylline is not recommended for claudication treatment.
population: Chronic symptomatic PAD
evidenceNote: Original recommendation class and evidence level retained.
cautions: Reference only; eligibility and contraindications require individual review.

title: PAD: nonwalking structured exercise
summary: Alternative structured exercise, such as arm ergometry or recumbent stepping, can improve function and walking performance.
population: Chronic symptomatic PAD
evidenceNote: Original recommendation class and evidence level retained.
cautions: Reference only; eligibility and contraindications require individual review.

title: Resistant hypertension: confirm the diagnosis before escalation
summary: Standardize BP measurement and assess adherence and other causes of difficult control before selecting escalation strategies.
population: Adults with apparent resistant hypertension
locator: Official ACC release, October 5, 2026: five-question framework
evidenceNote: No recommendation class assigned in the accessed official summary.
cautions: Complements the 2025 BP guideline; no medication sequence or renal-denervation eligibility is automated.

title: Hospital tobacco treatment: start varenicline
summary: CHEST recommends initiating varenicline during admission to support smoking cessation after discharge.
population: Hospitalized adults who smoke cigarettes.
locator: Official synopsis: Key Recommendations, first statement
evidenceNote: Public synopsis does not display formal strength or certainty; neither is inferred.
cautions: Review contraindications, renal dosing and continuity after discharge.

title: Hospital tobacco treatment: counseling
summary: Provide inpatient cessation counseling rather than brief advice; CHEST describes counseling lasting at least 15 minutes.
population: Hospitalized adults who smoke cigarettes.
locator: Key Recommendations, second statement; counseling-duration panel
evidenceNote: Formal strength and certainty are not displayed in the public synopsis.

title: After discharge: telephone cessation support
summary: Offer telephone-based cessation counseling after discharge rather than no follow-up counseling.
population: Hospitalized adults who smoke cigarettes.
locator: Official synopsis: Key Recommendations, third statement
evidenceNote: Formal strength and certainty are not displayed in the public synopsis.

title: CAP: shorter antibiotic course after stability
summary: For clinically stable adult outpatients, ATS suggests fewer than 5 antibiotic days, with a minimum of 3 days.
population: Adult outpatients with CAP who reach clinical stability.
evidenceNote: Low-quality evidence.
cautions: Individualize using daily stability assessment; complications, resistant pathogens and immunocompromise need separate guidance.

title: Nonsevere inpatient CAP: avoid routine steroids
summary: Do not routinely administer systemic corticosteroids for nonsevere inpatient CAP.
population: Adults hospitalized with nonsevere CAP.
evidenceNote: Low-quality evidence.
cautions: This addresses CAP treatment; another established steroid indication must be considered separately.

title: Severe inpatient CAP: consider steroids
summary: ATS suggests systemic corticosteroids for severe inpatient CAP, excluding influenza pneumonia.
population: Adults hospitalized with severe CAP.
evidenceNote: Low-quality evidence.
cautions: Check contraindications and severity; no single drug, dose or duration is established by this recommendation.

title: Septic shock or likely sepsis: immediate antibiotics
summary: Give antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 hour, for possible/probable/definite septic shock or probable/definite sepsis without shock.
population: Adults with septic shock or probable/definite sepsis.
locator: Antibiotic initiation: first and second strong recommendations
evidenceNote: Very low certainty.
cautions: Possible sepsis without shock has a separate assessment pathway; this is an acute-care reference.

title: Septic shock: first-line norepinephrine
summary: Use norepinephrine rather than dopamine, epinephrine or selepressin as the first vasopressor.
population: Adults with septic shock.
locator: Vasopressors: norepinephrine versus dopamine, epinephrine or selepressin
evidenceNote: High certainty versus dopamine; low versus epinephrine or selepressin.
cautions: Acute monitored care; other vasopressor comparisons carry different grades.

title: After sepsis: recovery follow-up
summary: Offer post-critical-illness follow-up services after sepsis hospitalization.
population: Adult sepsis or septic-shock survivors.
evidenceNote: Low certainty.
cautions: Tailor services to needs and resources; a fixed early follow-up interval is not established.

title: ICU stress-ulcer prophylaxis: reassess and stop
summary: Stop stress-ulcer prophylaxis once its bleeding-risk factors resolve; review it before transfer out of the ICU.
population: Critically ill adults receiving stress-ulcer prophylaxis.
locator: Cessation of SUP: first Good Practice Statement
evidenceNote: No graded certainty assigned.
cautions: Check for a separate ongoing indication for PPI or H2RA therapy.

title: Improving cUTI: shorter treatment courses
summary: For improving cUTI on effective therapy, use 5–7 days of a fluoroquinolone or 7 days of a non-fluoroquinolone rather than 10–14 days.
population: Adults with cUTI, including pyelonephritis, improving on effective therapy.
locator: Duration of Antibiotics for Complicated UTI, recommendation I; definitions and comments
evidenceNote: Moderate certainty for fluoroquinolones; very low for non-fluoroquinolones.
cautions: Count from first effective treatment day. Trials commonly excluded catheters, severe sepsis, immunocompromise, CKD, abscess, prostatitis, obstruction and urologic procedures; individualize.

title: Improving cUTI: transition from IV to oral
summary: Switch to an effective oral antibiotic when clinical improvement, oral intake and an appropriate oral option permit.
population: cUTI initially treated intravenously.
locator: Timing of Intravenous to Oral Antibiotics Transition, recommendation I; comments
evidenceNote: Low certainty.
cautions: Supporting trials generally required afebrile, hemodynamically stable patients with urinary obstruction relieved. Bacteremia requires adequate bloodstream and tissue exposure.

title: ESBL cUTI: susceptibility-directed treatment
summary: Susceptible TMP-SMX, ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin are preferred. If resistance, intolerance or toxicity prevents use, prefer a carbapenem or cefepime-enmetazobactam.
population: cUTI caused by ESBL-producing Enterobacterales.
evidenceNote: Clinical guidance; no formal GRADE strength or certainty assigned.
cautions: Choice requires organism susceptibility, infection site, severity, toxicity and specialist review; this is not a dosing or empiric-treatment protocol.

title: S. aureus bacteremia: document culture clearance
summary: Obtain at least 2 follow-up culture sets at 48 hours after the first positive sample, then 1–2 sets every 24–48 hours until negative.
population: Adults with S. aureus bacteremia.
locator: Consensus Statement 2, Adult Population Consensus Statement and remarks
evidenceNote: Consensus; not a formally graded recommendation.
cautions: Persistent positivity at 48 hours prompts deeper infection and source-control reassessment; monitoring may need intensification.

title: COPD: one exacerbation can prompt escalation
summary: Consider treatment escalation after one moderate exacerbation; GOLD 2026 lowers the prior exacerbation threshold.
population: Adults with COPD and a moderate exacerbation.
locator: Page 1, Key Changes item iv; references to Figures 3.7–3.9
evidenceNote: Observational evidence cited; no formal certainty category assigned in this summary.
cautions: Review the full follow-up pathway and prior therapy before choosing an inhaler.

title: COPD: initial versus follow-up treatment
summary: Use the initial pathway for maintenance-treatment-naïve COPD and the follow-up pathway for patients already receiving maintenance treatment.
population: Adults with COPD undergoing maintenance-treatment selection.
locator: Page 1, Key Changes item vi; Figures 3.7–3.9
evidenceNote: No formal certainty category assigned in this summary.

title: Mild asthma: as-needed ICS-formoterol
summary: Preferred initial treatment is as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol for infrequent symptoms or symptoms below 3–5 days weekly with normal/mildly reduced lung function.
population: Adults and adolescents with diagnosed asthma.
locator: Box 4-4, page 81, first and second symptom rows
evidenceNote: GINA Evidence A; not ACC/AHA Class I or LOE A.
cautions: Check diagnosis, device technique, local labeling and access; SABA-only care is not the preferred pathway.

title: Frequent asthma symptoms: low-dose MART
summary: Low-dose ICS-formoterol maintenance-and-reliever therapy is preferred for the Box 4-4 symptoms-most-days, weekly-waking or low-lung-function initial-treatment profile.
population: Adults/adolescents meeting Box 4-4 row 3, without features requiring a higher starting step.
locator: Box 4-4, page 81, third symptom row; compare fourth row for higher starting treatment
evidenceNote: GINA Evidence A.
cautions: Daily symptoms or weekly waking combined with low lung function or recent exacerbation prompts assessment for medium-dose MART instead.

title: Controlled asthma: supervised step-down
summary: Consider step-down after at least 3 months of stable control and lung function; avoid completely stopping ICS-containing therapy.
population: Adults/adolescents with controlled asthma.
locator: Box 4-13, page 112, general principles and Step 2 caution
evidenceNote: GINA Evidence D for timing; Evidence A for avoiding complete ICS cessation.
cautions: Use an action plan and follow-up; exacerbation risk may require closer supervision.

title: ADA: CGM with insulin therapy
summary: Recommend CGM from diabetes onset or later for adults using insulin; select the device around individual circumstances and preferences.
population: Adults with diabetes using insulin.
evidenceNote: Insulin-therapy clause: A; individualized device choice: E.
cautions: Device training and reliable access are needed.

title: ADA: CGM beyond insulin
summary: Recommend CGM for adults using noninsulin therapies that can cause hypoglycemia, or when CGM helps diabetes management.
population: Adults with diabetes.
evidenceNote: Both noninsulin clauses carry grade C.
cautions: Individualize device and use.

title: ADA obesity standards: medication choice with type 2 diabetes
summary: For overweight or obesity with type 2 diabetes, prefer a GLP-1 receptor agonist or dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist for weight and glycemic efficacy.
population: Adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes.
evidenceNote: ADA grade A; not an ACC/AHA class.
cautions: Check contraindications, approved indication, tolerability, and access.

title: AACE: choose diabetes treatment around complications
summary: Use comorbidities and complications, alongside glycemia, to guide initial and subsequent drug choices; address weight, blood pressure, and lipids concurrently.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes.
evidenceNote: No formal recommendation grade assigned to this consensus summary.
cautions: Use the complete algorithm for specific drug eligibility.

title: AACE: individualized A1c when using insulin
summary: Individualize glycemic targets; A1c ≤6.5% is recommended for most adults using insulin only when safely achievable with minimal or no hypoglycemia.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes using insulin.
locator: Initiating and Titrating Insulin Algorithm; Algorithm Figure 8
evidenceNote: No formal grade assigned in the reviewed consensus passage.
cautions: Reassess treatment burden and hypoglycemia risk.

title: Primary aldosteronism: broaden screening
summary: Suggest screening all people with hypertension using aldosterone and renin with the aldosterone-to-renin ratio; potassium helps interpretation.
population: People with hypertension.
evidenceNote: Low certainty (⊕⊕OO).
cautions: Feasibility, assay methods, potassium, and interfering drugs affect testing.

title: Confirmed primary aldosteronism: targeted treatment
summary: Suggest PA-specific treatment: MRA therapy for bilateral disease or nonsurgical patients; consider unilateral adrenalectomy for suitable patients with lateralizing disease who want surgery.
population: People with hypertension and confirmed primary aldosteronism.
evidenceNote: Low certainty (⊕⊕OO).
cautions: Confirm subtype and surgical suitability with specialist evaluation.

title: Long-term glucocorticoids: when to taper
summary: Attempt tapering long-term glucocorticoids only when the underlying disease is controlled and steroids are no longer needed; taper toward a physiologic dose before withdrawal assessment.
population: People taking long-term systemic glucocorticoids for nonendocrine disease.
evidenceNote: R 2.2 is good clinical practice, without a certainty grade.
cautions: Plan for adrenal-insufficiency risk; this is not a complete taper schedule.

title: Differentiated thyroid cancer: postoperative risk
summary: Use the 2025 ATA system with pathology and nodal findings, AJCC stage, postoperative imaging, and appropriate Tg/TgAb testing to estimate persistence or recurrence risk.
population: Adults after surgery for differentiated thyroid cancer.
evidenceNote: Moderate certainty.
cautions: Specialist interpretation is required.

title: Low-risk thyroid cancer: de-escalate ultrasound
summary: After total thyroidectomy plus RAI and a sustained excellent response for 5–8 years, routine ultrasound may stop; continue biochemical follow-up every 1–2 years.
population: Low-risk differentiated thyroid cancer with the specified treatment and sustained response.
evidenceNote: Low certainty.
cautions: New symptoms or biochemical changes may require imaging.

title: Pregnancy with hypothyroidism: levothyroxine alone
summary: Treat maternal hypothyroidism with levothyroxine monotherapy; avoid liothyronine and desiccated thyroid preparations during pregnancy.
population: Pregnant people with hypothyroidism requiring replacement.
evidenceNote: Low certainty; retained as ATA strength and certainty.
cautions: Coordinate dose and laboratory follow-up with pregnancy care.

title: KDIGO: SGLT2 with lower albuminuria
summary: Suggest an SGLT2 inhibitor when eGFR is 20–45 mL/min/1.73 m² and UACR is <200 mg/g.
population: Adults with established CKD, eGFR 20–45 mL/min/1.73 m² and UACR <200 mg/g.
evidenceNote: Moderate certainty.
cautions: Assess contraindications and medication safety.

title: KDIGO: nonsteroidal MRA eligibility
summary: Suggest a nonsteroidal MRA with proven benefit for T2D, eGFR >25, normal potassium, and albuminuria >30 mg/g despite maximum tolerated RAS inhibition.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD.
evidenceNote: High certainty.
cautions: eGFR units: mL/min/1.73 m²; monitor potassium.

title: Uncomplicated diverticulitis: selective antibiotics
summary: Suggest avoiding routine antibiotics in low-risk acute uncomplicated diverticulitis; antibiotics remain appropriate with high-risk features or unsafe outpatient management.
population: Adults with acute uncomplicated diverticulitis.
evidenceNote: Moderate certainty.
cautions: Nonantibiotic care requires immunocompetence, stability, oral intake, and reliable follow-up; exclude frailty and systemic inflammation.

title: Complicated diverticulitis: follow-up colonoscopy
summary: Recommend colonoscopy after recovery from complicated diverticulitis to exclude missed malignancy or premalignant lesions.
population: Adults recovering from complicated diverticulitis.
evidenceNote: Moderate certainty.
cautions: Avoid colonoscopy during the first 6–8 weeks after the acute episode.

title: H. pylori: confirm eradication
summary: Confirm cure at least 4 weeks after treatment using a breath, stool-antigen, or biopsy-based test; hold PPIs for 2 weeks and antibiotics/bismuth for 4 weeks.
population: People treated for H. pylori infection.
evidenceNote: No formal strength or certainty grade assigned to this highlighted key concept.
cautions: Arrange testing and medication instructions before treatment ends.

title: Constipation: evaluate pelvic floor dysfunction
summary: Before labeling chronic constipation refractory, most patients should undergo anorectal manometry and balloon-expulsion testing and complete pelvic-floor biofeedback when indicated.
population: Adults with chronic constipation.
evidenceNote: No formal quality or strength rating; systematic reviews were not performed.
cautions: Refer for appropriate physiologic testing.

title: Refractory constipation: review secondary causes
summary: Evaluate medication effects, disordered eating, and neurological or other secondary causes before escalating refractory-constipation treatment.
population: Adults with refractory constipation.
evidenceNote: No formal quality or strength rating.
cautions: Review clinically necessary drugs before changing them.

title: MASLD: stepwise fibrosis assessment
summary: Use noninvasive fibrosis assessment in two tiers, beginning with FIB-4; low-risk results generally permit primary-care management, while other results need additional assessment.
population: Adults evaluated through the MASLD risk-stratification pathway.
evidenceNote: No formal recommendation grade assigned in the official pathway summary.
cautions: FIB-4 does not diagnose MASH or determine drug eligibility alone.

title: HBV indeterminate phase: discuss antiviral therapy
summary: Suggest antivirals through shared decision-making for HBsAg-positive, HBeAg-negative indeterminate-phase HBV without cirrhosis; reassess the decision at follow-up.
population: Adults meeting the specified HBV phase and cirrhosis criteria.
evidenceNote: Very low certainty.
cautions: Confirm disease phase and evaluate other causes of liver injury.

title: HBV suppression: avoid routine antiviral withdrawal
summary: Suggest continuing nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy until HBsAg loss when HBeAg is negative, cirrhosis absent, and HBV DNA remains undetectable on treatment.
population: Adults with chronic HBV meeting these conditions.
evidenceNote: Very low certainty.
cautions: Exceptional withdrawal requires specialist shared decisions and close monitoring for flares.

title: MASH with F2–F3 fibrosis: semaglutide pathway
summary: The focused guidance supports considering semaglutide for adults with MASH and moderate-to-advanced fibrosis consistent with F2–F3, using appropriate fibrosis assessment.
population: Adults with noncirrhotic MASH and F2–F3 fibrosis.
locator: Patient selection; official November 2025 update announcement
strength: Practice guidance · grade not assigned in reviewed summary
evidenceNote: No formal strength or certainty rating assigned in the accessible summary.
cautions: Confirm diagnosis, contraindications, product labeling, and medication access.

title: Iron deficiency: adult ferritin threshold
summary: Use ferritin ≤30 ng/mL rather than ≤15 ng/mL to diagnose iron deficiency, with or without anemia.
population: Adults who are not menstruating or pregnant, without known or suspected inflammation.
evidenceNote: Low certainty; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Symptoms or continuing risk factors may justify a ≤50 ng/mL threshold. Inflammation requires a separate approach.

title: ITP: treatment after corticosteroids
summary: A thrombopoietic agent is recommended; rituximab is an alternative suggested option.
population: Adults with primary ITP needing additional treatment after initial corticosteroids, with or without IVIG.
strength: Strong for thrombopoietic agent; conditional for rituximab
evidenceNote: Moderate certainty for thrombopoietic agents; low for rituximab.
cautions: Coordinate with hematology. Rituximab may suit people seeking to avoid chronic therapy or unable to receive a thrombopoietic agent.

title: Surgery-provoked VTE: thrombophilia testing
summary: Do not routinely test for thrombophilia to decide anticoagulant duration after surgery-provoked VTE.
population: Patients who completed primary short-term treatment for surgery-provoked VTE.
evidenceNote: Very low certainty.
cautions: Do not extend this statement to every provoking factor; the guideline treats nonsurgical transient factors separately.

title: Cancer: review vaccination status
summary: Review vaccination status at diagnosis and bring seasonal, age-based and risk-based vaccines up to date.
population: Adults newly diagnosed with cancer and about to start treatment.
evidenceNote: Moderate-quality evidence.
cautions: Use current vaccine-specific schedules; transplant and cellular-therapy revaccination have separate pathways.

title: Cancer: timing nonlive vaccination
summary: Ideally vaccinate 2–4 weeks before planned treatment; nonlive vaccines can also be given during or after treatment.
population: Adults with cancer.
evidenceNote: Moderate-quality evidence.
cautions: Coordinate with oncology. This timing statement does not authorize live vaccines during immunosuppression.

title: Knee and hip OA: exercise and weight
summary: Recommend exercise; recommend weight loss when overweight or obesity is present.
population: People with knee or hip osteoarthritis.
evidenceNote: Moderate certainty for both recommendations.
cautions: Personalize the plan, accounting for function, comorbidities and treatment access.

title: Knee OA with obesity: GLP-1 RA
summary: Consider a GLP-1 receptor agonist with diet and exercise to support weight management.
population: People with knee osteoarthritis and obesity.
evidenceNote: Moderate certainty.
cautions: Assess drug-specific eligibility, contraindications and access; this does not establish a VA approval criterion.

title: Migraine: offer prevention
summary: Offer prevention with ≥4 migraine days/month, ≥4 moderate-to-severe headache days/month, or substantial migraine disability.
population: Adults with migraine.
evidenceNote: Native recommendation level; not an ACC/AHA evidence grade.
cautions: Select treatment with the patient after reviewing comorbidities, contraindications, pregnancy potential and interactions.

title: Migraine: allow time to assess prevention
summary: Assess most preventives after 8–12 weeks at a tolerated recommended dose; allow 24 weeks for onabotulinumtoxinA.
population: Adults receiving migraine preventive medication.
evidenceNote: Native recommendation level.
cautions: Tolerability and individual response can require earlier reassessment.

title: Functional seizures: medication review
summary: Avoid benzodiazepines for abortive treatment and antiseizure drugs solely for functional seizures; taper unnecessary antiseizure medication.
population: People with confirmed functional seizures without coexisting epilepsy or another medication indication.
evidenceNote: Native recommendation levels retained.
cautions: Confirm the diagnosis and other indications. Plan any taper with the treating clinician; do not abruptly stop dependence-forming drugs.

title: Breast screening: ACP ages 40–49
summary: Discuss benefits, harms, risk and preferences; if screening is chosen, use biennial mammography.
population: Asymptomatic average-risk females aged 40–49.
evidenceNote: No formal recommendation strength assigned.
cautions: Differs from USPSTF 2024, which recommends biennial screening starting at 40.

title: Breast screening: ACP ages 50–74
summary: Use mammography every two years.
population: Asymptomatic average-risk females aged 50–74.
evidenceNote: No formal recommendation strength assigned.
cautions: Symptoms or high-risk history require a separate pathway.

title: Pregnancy: early syphilis screening
summary: Screen universally as early as possible; if missed, screen at the first available opportunity.
population: All pregnant adolescents and adults, irrespective of risk factors.
evidenceNote: High certainty of substantial net benefit.
cautions: Evaluate and treat abnormal results promptly. This does not define repeat-testing requirements later in pregnancy.

title: Screen for intimate partner violence
summary: Screen for IPV and provide or refer positive screens to multicomponent interventions with ongoing support.
population: Women of reproductive age, including pregnant and postpartum women.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained.
cautions: Evidence is insufficient for routine caregiver-abuse screening in older or vulnerable adults; this is not a recommendation against evaluating suspected abuse.

title: HPV: catch-up through age 26
summary: Complete vaccination through age 26 if not adequately vaccinated. Starting at ≥15 years uses three doses at 0, 1–2 and 6 months.
population: Adults through age 26.
evidenceNote: No recommendation-specific certainty grade displayed.
cautions: A series begun before age 15 usually uses two doses 6–12 months apart; immunocompromised people need three doses.

title: HPV: shared decision ages 27–45
summary: Consider vaccination through shared decision making when prior vaccination is incomplete.
population: Adults aged 27–45.
evidenceNote: No recommendation-specific certainty grade displayed.
cautions: Prevents new infection; does not treat existing HPV disease. Benefit is smaller after prior exposure.

title: Hepatitis B: EASL treatment eligibility
summary: Treat chronic HBV with DNA ≥2,000 IU/mL plus elevated ALT and/or significant fibrosis.
population: HBeAg-positive or HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B.
evidenceNote: Native level of evidence 1; not mapped to ACC/AHA.
cautions: Cirrhosis and other special populations have separate criteria; assess with hepatology.

title: Hepatitis B: monitoring before treatment
summary: Monitor ALT and HBV DNA every 3–6 months during the first year or until treatment; thereafter individualize to 6–12 months by disease phase.
population: Newly diagnosed chronic HBV not yet receiving antivirals.
locator: Monitoring untreated chronic HBV recommendation table
evidenceNote: No numeric level assigned to this monitoring statement in the checked table.
cautions: Do not apply this interval to treated HBV or substitute it for cancer surveillance.

title: RA: prompt disease-modifying therapy
summary: Start a DMARD as soon as rheumatoid arthritis is diagnosed.
population: People with diagnosed rheumatoid arthritis.
evidenceNote: Native level of evidence 1a.
cautions: Coordinate treatment with rheumatology; this does not recommend DMARDs solely for positive autoantibodies.

title: RA: initial DMARD strategy
summary: Include methotrexate in the first treatment strategy; consider leflunomide or sulfasalazine for contraindication or early intolerance.
population: People with rheumatoid arthritis starting disease-modifying treatment.
evidenceNote: Native level of evidence 1a.
cautions: Specialist selection and drug-specific contraindication and monitoring review are required.
